correctness.rationale: The staggered transformation is exact; fixed-particle exclusion sectors are irreducible; the projected endpoint generator has exact binomial jump rates. Walsh–Krawtchouk eigenfunctions give every first-order rate and a symmetric finite-dimensional gap perturbation proves the O_N(epsilon^2) estimate. The mean K drift and sector occupancy formula establish slow-time and equilibrium claims. Exact finite checker passed 240 comparisons plus 18 optional spectral/slow-coverage comparisons. No growing-N uniform claim is made.

originality.rationale: The new assessed content is the first-order all-mode weak-bond spectral classification and the singular metastable coverage trajectory on odd rings. Uniform-bond sector counting and generic finite-dimensional perturbation are established tools and are excluded from novelty. Inspected closely related full-text model definitions do not directly imply the marked-bond result; one inaccessible 1994 defective-bond diffusion paper is a remaining nondecisive priority risk.
residual_risks: The full 1994 Chen–Stinchcombe defective-bond paper could not be inspected and may contain a reducible or broader limit.
The published and indexed literature search is not exhaustive; implicit coverage by a general reaction-diffusion spectral theorem remains possible.
The asymptotic is for fixed odd N as epsilon decreases; the coefficient cannot be asserted uniform in N.

value.rationale: Identifies the full family of slow rates, not just one coefficient, for physically motivated restoration of a broken ring bond. The Krawtchouk reduction explains the otherwise nonobvious universal 4/N spectral gap and gives an explicit delayed approach between two distinct coverage plateaux. This determines a natural finite-system relaxation invariant whose effect cannot be deduced from the previously published static density alone.
